messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a cluster of accounts flagged as "Low Health" but when I spot-checked CRM rows a lot of them are missing onboarding_date and primary_owner. Playbook automation is firing on those and creating noisy nudges.

maria: Example: 3 enterprise accounts (acct_id: 8421, 8429, 8433) got the "onboard_followup" playbook even though they're actually mid-onboard. Looks like the healthscore SQL treats NULL onboarding_date as stale and drops the score.

devon: ugh. probably the NULL handling in the healthscore calc. did we recently change the field mapping for onboarding_date -> onboarding.started_at?

aj: we migrated some contact imports last week. mapping change was in the ETL that writes to crm.accounts.onboard_meta. if the key is missing it becomes NULL.

leo: @maria can you paste the healthscore snippet? want to see how NULLs are weighted.

maria: sure — here's the simplified calc we think is causing it:
```sql
SELECT account_id,
  COALESCE(days_since(onboarding_date), 999) AS onboarding_days,
  CASE WHEN onboarding_days > 30 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS onboarding_flag,
  engagement_score * 0.6 + onboarding_flag * 0.4 AS health_score
FROM crm.accounts
WHERE account_tier != 'internal'
```

maria: so NULL -> COALESCE(,999) -> onboarding_flag 0 -> drags health_score down.

devon: minor tweak: treat NULL as unknown (neutral) not stale. e.g. COALESCE(days_since(onboarding_date), 15) or add a separate unknown bucket.

aj: agree. but playbook automation triggers are based on health_score threshold. we could also change trigger to require last_touch < 14 AND health_score < 0.4, that would reduce false positives for accounts with missing metadata.

leo: good call. also we should fix the import to ensure onboarding.started_at is backfilled when present in payload. I can add a quick reconciliation job that copies event logs -> onboarding_date for last 90 days.

maria: action items: 1) change NULL handling in scoring (devon) 2) tighten playbook trigger (aj) 3) run a backfill for recent imports (leo) 4) dry-run playbook suppression for 24h to avoid more noisy nudges (maria)

devon: will open a small PR for score calc with tests. plan: default unknown -> 15 days and add flag `onboarding_unknown` so downstream can opt-in.

aj: i'll update playbook config in ops repo, add new condition `not onboarding_unknown` for automatic nudges and put it behind a feature flag. will link PR here.

csops-bot: deploy-check — branch=cs/playbook-tighten, status=ok, queued-reviewers=[aj,devon], CI=passing

leo: starting the backfill job now against staging. will run a sample and post counts.

maria: sample from staging after backfill scan: 178 accounts missing onboarding_date -> 0 events found in event_log last 90d for 24 of them; the rest have events we can backfill.

devon: thanks. i'll aim to get PR up by EOD. tagging @aj for the feature flag rollout plan — we should phase it on for trial and seed segments first.

aj: noted. will do phased rollout: 1) seeding only, 2) trials, 3) general. will enable suppression for 24h immediately after deploy.

maria: can we add a quick monitoring alert for playbook firing rate? if suppression isn't working we should catch it fast.

leo: yep — adding metric `playbook.onboard_followup.fires_per_min` and alert if >5x baseline for 10m.

maria: thanks all. putting this into the CS ops board as a ticket and assigning to respective owners. i'll follow up with a short postmortem once we've validated the backfill and rollout. :thumbsup:

devon: small note — for long-term, we should avoid encoding semantics into NULL handling. better to add explicit enums (unknown/stale/complete) in the ETL and surface them to the healthscore.

aj: yep, long-term roadmap item. created a backlog card.

leo: backfill finished on staging: 154 accounts patched, 24 still manual. will schedule a small support tagging run for the remaining.

maria: great. closing loop: suppression dry-run on for 24h, PRs linked, monitoring added. will reopen if anything else crops up.

maria: thanks everyone.
